mainTopic: The placement and use of the tables and מנורות in the מקדש, the rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין, and honoring a תלמיד חכם who forgot his learning
overview: The גמרא first checks whether שלמה's ten tables and משה's שלחן can all fit in the north half of the היכל. If the tables ran צפון ודרום, everything fits. If they ran מזרח ומערב, the measurements seem to push the שלחן half an אמה into the south. The גמרא answers that משה's שלחן was not in the same row. It stood higher, and שלמה's tables sat a little lower, like a student before his teacher. Next a ברייתא argues over whether the לחם הפנים was placed only on משה's table and only משה's מנורה was lit, or whether all of them were used. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה explains the plural 'tables' as three tables: silver and gold ones in the אולם, and the gold שלחן inside. This follows the rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין. The גמרא then gives a separate פסוק as the source for each half of that rule. From the broken לוחות kept in the ארון, it learns that a תלמיד חכם who forgot his learning through אונס must still be honored. It ends with a memory aid for three teachings of ריש לקיש, the first of which begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The north-south opinion works out fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that according to the opinion that the tables were placed צפון ודרום, the arrangement fits well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who said the tables ran north to south, it works out well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that one opinion has no problem. This is a setup line: it prepares a difficulty against the other opinion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא signals a contrast. One side is fine, and the other side is about to be challenged. Here the tables run across the width of the היכל, so there is room for the כהנים on the east and west sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it is understandable (opens a contrast before a difficulty)
Well / it works out fine
North and south (the tables ran along the width of the היכל)

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said
north and south, it works out well.
phrases.notes: He means the tables were lined up running from north to south.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר צָפוֹן וְדָרוֹם, שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the challenge by granting the first opinion before attacking the second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to צפון ודרום, the layout of the tables has no difficulty.

steps.title: Measuring the space from the northern wall
steps.stepSummary: According to the מזרח ומערב opinion, the גמרא starts adding up how much room the tables take, beginning from the northern wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who said east and west: how far is the Table from the wall? Two and a half cubits, plus one cubit for the row itself, plus two and a half cubits of space in between.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its challenge against the מזרח ומערב opinion by measuring the space step by step from the northern wall. The calculation continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First there are two and a half אמות of open space from the wall. Then one אמה for the width of the northern row of tables. Then another two and a half אמות of open space. The open spaces leave room for the כהנים, who stand on the north and south sides of the tables in this opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: East and west (the tables ran along the length of the היכל)
Now, consider (opens a logical calculation)
Wall
Cubit, a unit of measurement
In between

phrases.english: But according to the one who said east and west,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי שֻׁלְחָן כַּמָּה מָשׁוּךְ מִן הַכּוֹתֶל?
phrases.english: now, how far is the Table removed from the wall?
phrases.notes: The wall here is the northern wall of the היכל.

phrases.english: Two and a half cubits,
and its own cubit,
phrases.notes: This is the one-cubit width of the northern row of tables.

phrases.english: and two and a half cubits that are in between.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the opinion that works to the opinion that seems to have a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the tables ran מזרח ומערב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding up the spaces and table widths will show that the tables cannot all fit in the north half of the היכל.

steps.title: The total spills half a cubit into the south
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the count and finds that the tables would take ten and a half אמות, so the שלחן would reach half an אמה into the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a cubit, and two and a half cubits in between, and one cubit for the row itself. It turns out that the Table occupies half a cubit in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the measurement and shows the problem: the tables run past the middle of the היכל into the southern half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full total is 2.5 + 1 + 2.5 + 1 (משה's שלחן) + 2.5 + 1 (southern row) = 10.5 אמות. The היכל is twenty אמות wide, so its north half is only ten. That leaves half an אמה in the south, but the שלחן belongs in the north.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out / it is found
Literally 'eats', meaning takes up or occupies space
Half a cubit

steps.confusionAlert: Don't lose track of what each אמה stands for. The first new אמה here is the width of משה's שלחן in the middle, and the last one is the width of the southern row of tables.

phrases.english: And a cubit,
phrases.notes: This is the width of משה's Table in the middle.

phrases.english: and two and a half cubits that are in between,
and its own cubit —
phrases.notes: Now this is the width of the southern row of tables.

phrases.english: it turns out that the Table occupies
half a cubit in the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתְּכַח דְּקָאָכֵיל שׁוּלְחָן פַּלְגָא דְּאַמְּתָא בְּדָרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the calculation begun in step 2 and states the difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the tables ran מזרח ומערב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The total width of 10.5 אמות is more than the 10-אמה north half, so the שלחן would partly stand in the south. That contradicts its required place in the north.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole challenge depends on the rule that the שלחן must be in the northern half of the היכל.

steps.title: משה's Table was set higher, not in the same row
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that משה's שלחן was not lined up beside the other tables. It was raised and placed apart, and the tables of שלמה were set a bit lower, like a student before his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think the Table of משה sat together with them? No. It was raised and placed, and they were lowered slightly, like a student who sits before his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty by saying the calculation was wrong to count משה's שלחן in the same line as the other tables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once משה's שלחן is not counted in the same row, its width no longer belongs in the side-by-side total, so the tables no longer spill into the south. The tables of שלמה sat slightly lower than משה's שלחן, showing respect, like a student sitting before his רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (introduces a wrong assumption being corrected)
The Table made by משה in the מדבר
Raised up
A little / slightly
Like a student sitting before his teacher

steps.whatToRemember: The difficulty disappears because משה's שלחן was not in the same row as שלמה's tables. It stood higher and apart, so its width is not added, and all the tables fit in the north.

phrases.english: Do you think that the Table of Moses
was sitting together with them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the ten tables that שלמה made.

phrases.english: No; it was raised and placed,
and they were lowered slightly,
like a student who sits before his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ שֻׁלְחָן דְּמֹשֶׁה בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ הֲוָה יָתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a hidden assumption about the layout
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge assumed משה's שלחן stood in the same row as שלמה's tables, so its width was added to the total.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה's שלחן was raised and set apart, so its width is not counted, and everything fits in the north half.

steps.title: Ten tables, but the bread went only on משה's table
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that שלמה made ten tables, but the לחם הפנים was placed only on משה's table, based on a פסוק that says 'the table' in singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: שלמה made ten tables, but they arranged the bread only on the table of משה, as it says: 'And the table upon which was the לחם הפנים, of gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that asks a new question: which of the tables actually held the לחם הפנים? The first opinion says only משה's table did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know there were ten extra tables. Now we learn they were not all used for the bread. The proof is that the פסוק speaks of 'the table', one table, holding the לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Tables
They arrange (the bread on the table)
The special bread kept on the שלחן
The one made by משה (in the מדבר)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Solomon made ten tables,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מְסַדְּרִין אֶלָּא עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: but they would arrange [the bread] only on the one of Moses,
as it says: 'And the table upon which'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 7:48. Notice the word 'table' is singular.

phrases.english: was the shewbread, of gold.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן עשרה שלחנות עשה שלמה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After placing the tables, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about which table was actually used for the bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לחם הפנים was arranged only on משה's table.

steps.title: Ten מנורות, but only משה's was lit
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא says שלמה made ten מנורות, but only משה's מנורה was lit, based on a פסוק that says 'the מנורה' in singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה made ten מנורות, but they lit only the one of משה, as it says: 'The golden מנורה and its lamps, to burn in the evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and says the same thing about the מנורות. There were ten, but only משה's was lit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the tables. The proof again comes from a singular word in the פסוק, 'the מנורה', which shows only one was lit.

keyTerms.meaning: Candelabra (more than one מנורה)
They light
To burn, to light

phrases.english: Solomon made ten candelabra,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁל מֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: but they would light only the one of Moses,
as it says: 'The golden candelabrum'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 13:11. Again, 'candelabrum' is singular.

phrases.english: and its lamps, to burn in the evening.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same rule from the tables to the מנורות.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע: all tables and all מנורות were used
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע disagrees. He says the bread was placed on all the tables and all the מנורות were lit, based on פסוקים that speak in plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע says: they arranged bread on all of them, as it says: 'The tables, and upon them the לחם הפנים.' And they lit all of them, as it says: 'The מנורות and their lamps, to burn them as required before the דביר, of pure gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא argues with the first. It says every table and every מנורה was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion read the singular פסוקים. רבי אלעזר בן שמוע points to other פסוקים that say 'tables' and 'מנורות' in plural, which suggests all of them were in use. So now we have a מחלוקת built on פסוקים that seem to point different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: On all of them
As required, according to the rule
The inner room, the קדש הקדשים
Pure (closed, refined) gold

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides quote פסוקים about שלמה's מקדש. The fight is over whether the singular פסוקים or the plural פסוקים describe how the tables and מנורות were actually used.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua says:
they would arrange [the bread] on all of them,
as it says: 'The tables'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 4:19. Here 'tables' is plural.

phrases.english: and upon them the shewbread,'
and they would light all of them,
as it says: 'The candelabra and their lamps,'
to burn them as required
before the Sanctuary, of pure gold.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע אומר על כולם היו מסדרין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the first opinion and says all the tables and מנורות were used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread was arranged on all the tables, and all the מנורות were lit.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: bread only on משה's table
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה sides with the first opinion: the bread was arranged only on משה's table.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: they arranged bread only on the table of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: A third voice in the ברייתא agrees with the first opinion about the tables. This sets up his explanation of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע's plural פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ruling is the same as the first opinion. What he adds is coming next: a way to explain the plural 'tables' without saying all of them held bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Only on the one of משה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מְסַדְּרִין אֶלָּא עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: they would arrange [the bread] only on the one of Moses,

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה אומר לא היו מסדרין אלא על של משה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first opinion against רבי אלעזר בן שמוע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only משה's table held the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Then what does the plural 'tables' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה asks himself how to explain the פסוק that speaks of 'tables' with the bread, in plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain: 'And the tables upon which was the לחם הפנים, of gold'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה raises the obvious difficulty with his own view. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural פסוק is the main support for רבי אלעזר בן שמוע. If only one table held the bread, the word 'tables' needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain (literally, how do I uphold) this פסוק?

phrases.english: But how do I explain
'And the tables upon which'
phrases.notes: This is the same plural פסוק רבי אלעזר בן שמוע used (דברי הימים ב 4:19–20).

phrases.english: was the shewbread, of gold'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the plural פסוק as a difficulty for the ruling just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to read the plural 'tables' if only משה's table held the bread.

steps.title: The 'tables' are three other tables in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה answers that the plural 'tables' refers to three tables in the מקדש, starting with two in the אולם, one of silver and one of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are three tables that were in the מקדש: two were in the אולם, on the inside, near the entrance to the בית, one of silver and one of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: He answers his question. The plural 'tables' means other tables that held the bread at other stages, not ten tables in use at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word now has a different meaning, so it no longer proves that all of שלמה's tables were used. This keeps the singular reading for משה's table. Two of the three tables are described here, both in the אולם near the doorway.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The doorway into the היכל
Silver

phrases.english: These are three tables
that were in the Temple:
two that were in the Entrance Hall
on the inside, by the entrance to the House,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: one of silver and one of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the plural פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'tables' refers to three special tables in the מקדש, two of them in the אולם (silver and gold), not to all ten of שלמה's tables.

steps.title: How the silver and gold tables are used, and the third table inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה explains the purpose of the two tables in the אולם and names the third table, the gold one inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the silver table the כהן puts the fresh לחם הפנים as it comes in. On the gold table he puts the old bread as it goes out, because we raise things up in holiness and do not bring them down. The third is the one gold table inside, which always has the לחם הפנים on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה finishes the answer he started in Step 10. He explains what the silver and gold tables in the אולם are used for, and then names the third table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new bread first rests on silver, then goes up to the gold שולחן inside. When it comes out, it has already been on gold, so it cannot go back down to silver. That is the rule of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין. This completes the count of 'three tables' that explains the plural word 'tables' in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: In holy matters we go up in level, never down
Bringing in / taking out
Inside (the היכל, the inner sanctuary)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three tables: silver in the אולם for new bread coming in, gold in the אולם for old bread going out, and משה's gold שולחן inside. The order follows the rule that we raise in holiness and never lower.
steps.confusionAlert: The gold table in the אולם is for the OLD bread on its way out, not the new bread. That is the opposite of what you might guess, and it is exactly the point: once the bread has been on gold, it cannot go down to silver.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין introduced here becomes the topic of the next several steps, and it shows up across many areas of הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁל כֶּסֶף נוֹתֵן לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ,
phrases.english: On the silver one he places the shewbread when it is brought in,
and on the gold one when it is taken out,
phrases.notes: This is the second gold table, the one in the אולם, not the main שולחן inside.

phrases.english: because we raise up in holiness and do not bring down.
And one of gold is inside,
on which the shewbread is always placed.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל שֶׁל כֶּסֶף נוֹתֵן לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 10 by explaining the two outer tables and naming the third.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'tables' refers to three tables: silver in the אולם for incoming bread, gold in the אולם for outgoing bread, and the gold שולחן inside, which always holds the bread.

steps.title: Where do we learn that we don't lower in holiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that holy things are not brought down in level.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that we do not lower in holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the rule just mentioned and asks for its source, starting with the 'don't lower' half. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 used the rule without proving it. The גמרא now wants a פסוק behind the idea that something holy cannot be moved to a lower level.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
We do not lower (in holiness)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we do not lower?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the 'do not lower' rule used in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source for the rule אין מורידין בקודש.

steps.title: Source from משה setting up the משכן
steps.stepSummary: רבי brings the פסוק describing משה putting up every part of the משכן as the source for 'we don't lower.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: The פסוק says: 'And משה set up the משכן, and he put its sockets, and placed its boards, and put in its bars, and set up its pillars.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers Step 12 with a פסוק showing משה doing every stage of building the משכן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק keeps saying that משה did each part. The usual explanation is that once משה, the greatest person, began the job, it was not handed down to anyone of lower stature. That is the idea of not lowering in holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tabernacle built in the desert
Silver sockets that held up the boards
The wooden boards forming the walls
Bars that held the boards together

phrases.english: Rabbi said: As the verse states:
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא. The פסוק is שמות 40:18.

phrases.english: 'And Moses erected the Tabernacle,
and he laid its sockets,
and set up its boards,
and put in its bars,
and erected its pillars.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק shows משה doing the whole building himself, so a holy task, once begun at a high level, is not passed down to a lower one.

steps.title: Where do we learn that we raise in holiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks for the source of the other half of the rule: that holy things may be raised up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that we raise up in holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the 'raise up' half of the rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not lowering is one idea. Actively raising something to a higher level of holiness is a separate idea, so it needs its own proof.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise up (in holiness)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we raise up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question to Step 12, now about the 'raise up' half of the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source for the rule מעלין בקודש.

steps.title: Source from the fire-pans of קרח's group
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר יעקב proves 'we raise up' from the fire-pans of קרח's group, which went from being tools of the מזבח to being part of the מזבח itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר יעקב said: The פסוק says, 'The fire-pans of these sinners against their own souls, let them be made into hammered sheets as a covering for the מזבח, because they offered them before ה׳ and they became holy, and they shall be a sign for בני ישראל.' At first they were tools of the מזבח, and now they are the body of the מזבח itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא בר יעקב answers Step 14. The fire-pans were moved up from being vessels used for the מזבח to being part of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire-pans had a lower holiness as תשמישי מזבח, tools used in the service. By being hammered into the מזבח's covering, they became גופו של מזבח, the מזבח itself. That move upward is the proof that we raise in holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire-pans used to burn incense
Hammered-out metal sheets
Tools used in the service of the מזבח
The actual body of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for one rule. 'Don't lower' comes from משה building the משכן himself. 'Raise up' comes from the fire-pans that became the מזבח's covering.

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
As the verse states:
phrases.notes: במדבר 17:3, about the fire-pans of קרח's group.

phrases.english: 'The fire-pans of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives,
let them be made into beaten plates
as a covering for the altar,
for they brought them before the Lord, and they became holy,
and they shall be a sign for the children of Israel.'
At first they were articles used for the altar,
and now they are the altar itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fire-pans went from tools of the מזבח to the body of the מזבח, which proves that holy items may be raised in level.

steps.title: The broken לוחות were kept in the ארון
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches from a פסוק that both the whole לוחות and the pieces of the broken first לוחות were placed in the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Which you broke, and you shall put them in the ארון.' רב יוסף taught: This teaches that the לוחות and the broken pieces of the לוחות were both placed in the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching about honoring holy things. Even the broken first לוחות kept their place inside the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'them' in the פסוק is read as including the broken pieces just mentioned. So the broken לוחות were not thrown away. They stayed in the holiest place, next to the new ones, because their holiness was not lowered.

keyTerms.meaning: The stone tablets of the עשרת הדברות
The broken pieces of the first tablets
The Holy Ark
This teaches (introduces a lesson drawn from a פסוק)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching that follows the theme of not lowering holy things.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the whole לוחות and the broken first לוחות were kept in the ארון.

steps.title: Respect for a תלמיד חכם who forgot his learning
steps.stepSummary: From the broken לוחות, the גמרא learns that a תלמיד חכם who forgot his learning because of circumstances beyond his control must not be treated with disrespect.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn about a תלמיד חכם who forgot his learning because of circumstances beyond his control: we do not treat him in a disrespectful way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical lesson from the broken לוחות in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broken לוחות kept their honored place even though they were no longer whole. In the same way, a תלמיד חכם who lost his learning through אונס, something not his fault, keeps his honor. He is compared to the broken לוחות.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar
Circumstances beyond one's control (such as illness)
Disrespectful treatment
From here (we learn)

steps.whatToRemember: Holiness is not taken away by damage that is not someone's fault. The broken לוחות stayed in the ארון, and a תלמיד חכם who forgot his learning through אונס keeps his honor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a fact about the ארון into a lasting rule of how we must treat people, especially elderly or ill Torah scholars.

phrases.english: From here we learn regarding a Torah scholar
who forgot his learning due to circumstances beyond his control,
that one may not treat him in a degrading manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁשָּׁכַח תַּלְמוּדוֹ מֵחֲמַת אוֹנְסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from the teaching in Step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A תלמיד חכם who forgot his learning through אונס is like the broken לוחות and must still be treated with honor.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next three teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a three-word סימן to help remember the order of ריש לקיש's three upcoming teachings: ביטל, סרח, and שכח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next teachings by giving a short memory aid. It is not teaching a law yet; it lists keywords so we can remember what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one teaching of ריש לקיש that comes next: ביטל (stopping Torah learning), סרח (a scholar who sinned), and שכח (a scholar who forgot). They connect to the theme of step 17, how we treat a תלמיד חכם, especially one who forgot his learning.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid; a short list of keywords to remember the order of teachings
He stopped or set aside (here, Torah learning)
He sinned or went wrong
He forgot (his learning)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a teaching or a law. It is only a list of keywords for the three statements that follow.

phrases.english: (Memory aid: 'stopped,' 'sinned,' 'and forgot.')
phrases.notes: Each word is a hint to one of the three teachings of ריש לקיש that come right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the lesson from the broken לוחות about a תלמיד חכם who forgot, the גמרא introduces a group of related teachings by ריש לקיש with a memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; this is a keyword list for three upcoming teachings: ביטל, סרח, שכח.

steps.title: ריש לקיש begins his first teaching
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש opens his first teaching (the ביטל teaching) with the word 'Sometimes.' The rest of his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש starts the first of the three teachings from the memory aid. Only the opening word is here; the full statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the 'ביטל' teaching from the memory aid, so it deals with setting aside Torah learning. The word 'Sometimes' tells us he is about to describe a special situation, different from the usual case.
